**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Stems (lower) and root system
- **Key features**:
  - Two plant stems are shown pulled from the soil, appearing to be split/cut longitudinally to expose internal tissue
  - The interior vascular tissue shows clear **brown streaking/discoloration** running through the lower stem
  - The root system is extensive and brown/dead-looking
  - The upper stem portions remain green, while the lower stem transitions sharply to tan/brown discoloration
  - No white mycelium, sclerotia, or spore masses are visible
  - No external cankers with concentric rings

**Reasoning:**

The key diagnostic feature here is the **brown vascular discoloration visible when stems are cut/split lengthwise**, along with the root system showing browning. This is the classic presentation of **Verticillium Wilt**, whose description specifically states: *"brown vascular discoloration visible when stems are cut lengthwise, and one-sided wilting due to asymmetric vascular colonization."*

- **Southern Bacterial Wilt** was considered but lacks the bacterial ooze streaming test and the discoloration here appears more in the vascular/pith rather than a slimy bacterial mass
- **Southern Blight** was ruled out — no white cottony mycelium or spherical sclerotia at the stem base
- **Alternaria Stem Cankers** was ruled out — no concentric rings on external cankers

The longitudinal cut showing internal brown vascular streaking from the lower stem upward is the hallmark of Verticillium wilt in tomato/solanaceous crops.
